title: Staged Traffic Shadowing with Budgeted Tenant Quarantine and Sampling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We need a safe, low-cost way to run production shadowing for new model variants across multiple tenants without risking runaway charges or cross-tenant data bleed. Existing lightweight sampling is ad hoc, and both cost and tenant isolation failures have been a recurring source of incidents. Goal: implement a staged shadowing controller that applies per-tenant budget fences, multi-stage sampling (initial micro-sample -> ramp -> steady-state), and automatic tenant quarantine + auto-rollback triggers when anomalies or overspend are detected. The feature should integrate with the routing layer, support both streaming and non-streaming requests, and emit detailed telemetry for cost attribution and quality comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can create staged shadowing policies scoped to tenant, route, and model-version
Per-tenant budget fence prevents shadowing beyond configured spend or token limit and emits a quota-exhausted event
Sampling supports deterministic micro-sample (0.1%) and ramp profiles up to a max safe sample (configurable), with stable randomization key to enable consistent per-session sampling
Shadowed responses are stored in S3-compatible blob with tenant-scoped encryption and retention controls and do not affect live latency SLOs
Automatic tenant quarantine triggers when either cost overrun (>20% above projection) or metric drift detected (1.5x baseline error rate) and disables shadowing for that tenant
Observability: per-tenant/per-policy dashboards show tokens consumed, sample rate, fail-rate, and cost estimate; alerts fire for budget threshold breaches
E2E test coverage includes sampling correctness, budget enforcement, quarantine behavior, and rollback on drift detection
Documentation and Console UI: policy editor + preview + rollout visualization available in Console before GA
implementation_notes: Controller model: declarative ShadowPolicy CR-like object persisted in config-store, reconciler in routing service applies sampling and cost checks
Sampling algorithm: use stable hashing on request.session_id or request.client_id to ensure consistent selection across retries and streaming chunks
Budget fencing: two dimensions - token budget and monetary budget; token budget counts shadowed tokens via runtime counters; monetary budget uses token->cost conversion using model profile rates
Tenant isolation: all shadow outputs stored under tenant-prefixed paths with SSE-KMS encryption. No unscoped debugging endpoints expose other tenants' data
Async writeback: shadow writes must never block main request path. Use write-behind queue with backpressure protection; if queue saturates, fall back to drop-mode and emit metric
Backpressure strategy: queue bounded by tenant and global caps; when saturated, decrement sample rate for affected tenants by policy-defined step
Auto-quarantine triggers: cost_exceeded, error_drift, or storage_flood. Quarantine lifecycle: disable shadowing -> notify tenant owners -> schedule safe re-enable window with reduced sampling
Rollback vs Quarantine: rollback affects rollout policies (canary canary->previous model) while quarantine only stops shadowing for tenant(s); both can be automated via the controller
Security: ensure only users with rollout role can create policies; audit events for policy changes logged to customer audit store for Private deployments
Telemetry: emit events for sample_decision, write_enqueued, write_failed, budget_consumed, quarantine_started, quarantine_ended with tenant_id and policy_id tags
Cost modeling: integrate with Optimize recommendations to suggest safe max sample and expected monthly spend for proposed policy
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged deploy to staging with synthetic traffic harness for 2 weeks
Phase 1: limit to internal tenants (redwood-dev-*) at micro-sampling 0.05% and validate storage/writes/metrics
Phase 2: opt-in beta customers (3 tenants) with controlled budget fences and 0.5% sample
Phase 3: gradual ramp to 1-2% across more tenants using automated ramp with daily budget checks
Phase 4: GA: expose policy editor in Console and enable per-account suggestions from Optimize
Safety gates: circuit-break on any >10% increase in end-to-end request latency attributable to shadow pipeline; block GA until resolved
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling hashing, budget accounting, and quota exhaustion logic
Integration tests: end-to-end request flows for streaming and non-streaming requests ensuring main path latency unaffected
Chaos tests: force writer queue saturation and validate graceful sample backoff and alerting
Load tests: simulate 1M requests/day per tenant to measure token counting and cost attribution accuracy
Security tests: RBAC checks and KMS access validations for private deployments
E2E validation runbook for SRE with steps to simulate budget breach and verify quarantine + recovery
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow writes could saturate storage or increase egress cost. Mitigation: per-tenant and global write quotas + drop-mode + alerting
Risk: Sampling drift could bias selection. Mitigation: use stable hashing keyed on immutable session id and validate sample distribution daily
Risk: Quarantine triggers too aggressively causing loss of observability. Mitigation: implement hysteresis windows and require multi-signal confirmation before quarantine
Risk: Incorrect cost model leading to under/over-fencing. Mitigation: conservative default conversion rates, and surface expected vs actual spend in Console
Risk: Privacy/regulatory exposure from storing shadow responses. Mitigation: tenant-scoped encryption, configurable PII redaction hooks before write
